claims.subject: tamil_kanthan
claims.summary: In the sages’ story, King Kānthan chooses Kahandan, described as a courtesan’s son, to rule while he leaves the city.
claims.speaker: Sages narrating to the king
claims.note: This supplies a passage-supported second edge from the Agastya-related Kānthan episode. It is not evidence of a meeting between Agastya and Kahandan.

claims.subject: tamil_kanthan
claims.summary: Kānthan tells Kahandan that Paraśurāma will not come to fight him because he was not born to a king; Kānthan separately says he plans to seek Agastya’s grace.
claims.speaker: King Kānthan in quoted speech
claims.note: Agastya is only the intended object of Kānthan’s visit in this episode; the passage does not narrate their encounter. Paraśurāma is a named person in Kānthan’s reported expectation, not a participant in the scene.

search_log.query: Bhāgavata Purāṇa Agastya 8.4.7–10, Maṇimēkalai canto 22, Buddhacarita 4.73 named people
search_log.outcome: Checked the primary translations. Bhāgavata 8.4.7–10 adds no new named individual beyond graph witnesses Indradyumna and Agastya; the disciples are unnamed and Śuka’s narration is not an Agastya encounter. Maṇimēkalai 22:30–40 adds named Kahandan and Paraśurāma via Kānthan’s story. Buddhacarita 4.73 names Agastya, Soma, Rohiṇī, and Lopāmudrā, all already represented in the graph; it is Udāyin’s analogy to the prince, not a narrated encounter with Agastya.

search_log.query: Project Madurai Maṇimēkalai Hart canto 22 lines 22-030–22-040
search_log.outcome: Checked Hart’s English passage. Added Kahandan and Paraśurāma with claims scoped to what the sages and Kānthan say.
Checked verses 7–10; elephant transformation is stated, but this passage supplies no additional named individual to add. Existing graph already records Indradyumna and the curse.
Checked Cowell translation hosted with the Sanskrit text. The verse is a reported traditional example inside Udāyin’s speech; no new named person was found.

notes: No new Bhāgavata Purāṇa or Buddhacarita nodes were warranted after comparing their named individuals against graph.json and existing expansion files.

The Tamil additions are two passage-supported persons in the Kānthan episode, within two narrative edges of Agastya’s intended visit: Agastya is named as the intended source of grace, Kānthan appoints Kahandan and speaks of Paraśurāma. These claims do not assert that Agastya met either person.
All entries are translation_checked, not original-language reviewed.
